title: HTTP Content Negotiation and Error Formats: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on how HTTP clients and servers agree on representation: Accept and Content-Type, media types, 406 vs 415, JSON vs other formats, Accept-Encoding compression, and Problem Details (RFC 9457) errors.

chapters.title: Negotiation Mental Model
points: Content negotiation: client states what it can handle, server picks a representation of the same resource; one URL, many formats
Accept (request) = formats I want back; Content-Type (request or response) = format of the body being sent; Accept-Encoding = compressions I can decode
Content-Type describes the body in this message; Accept describes the preferred response. Mixing them up is the top header bug
Server-driven negotiation is the norm; the server should add Vary: Accept (and Vary: Accept-Encoding) so caches key correctly
Interview Point: Q1 What is the difference between Accept and Content-Type? Q2 Who decides the final representation? Q3 Why does Vary matter for caches?

chapters.title: Media Types and Accept Rules
points: Media type syntax: type/subtype;param, e.g. application/json, text/html;charset=utf-8, image/png
Vendor types: application/vnd.company.v2+json; the +json suffix says the structure is JSON; used for versioning and custom schemas
Accept lists options with q-values (0 to 1, default 1): Accept: application/json, text/html;q=0.8, */*;q=0.1
Specificity wins over wildcards: application/json beats application/* beats */* when q is equal
JSON needs no charset parameter (always UTF-8); omit ;charset=utf-8 for application/json but include it for text/* types
Interview Point: Q1 How do q-values resolve a tie? Q2 What does +json in a vendor type mean? Q3 When would you version via media type instead of URL?

chapters.title: 406, 415 and Choosing Formats
points: 406 Not Acceptable: server cannot produce anything matching Accept; it is about the response format (header: Accept)
415 Unsupported Media Type: server will not read the request body's Content-Type; it is about the request format
Quick memory: 406 = I can't give you that; 415 = I can't take that. A missing or wrong Content-Type on POST usually causes 415
Many APIs ignore an unsatisfiable Accept and return default JSON rather than 406; both are allowed, pick one and document it

JSON vs others: JSON is the default for APIs (universal, human-readable); XML for legacy/SOAP; Protobuf/MessagePack for compact binary; CSV for tabular export; multipart/form-data for file uploads; application/x-www-form-urlencoded for simple forms
Interview Point: Q1 When do you return 406 vs 415? Q2 Why might POST with JSON body return 415? Q3 When choose Protobuf over JSON?

chapters.title: Compression with Accept-Encoding
points: Client sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, br, zstd; server replies with Content-Encoding: gzip (the one it chose) and Vary: Accept-Encoding
Content-Encoding is the compression of the body; Content-Type stays the original type (application/json), not application/gzip
gzip = universal default; br (Brotli) = better ratio for text, slower to compress, best for static assets; zstd = fast with good ratio, newer support
Compress text formats (JSON, HTML, CSS, JS, XML); skip already-compressed ones (JPEG, PNG, MP4, ZIP) and tiny bodies under about 1 KB

Test with curl --compressed -i https://api.example.com/items, or curl -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' --output - ; avoid compressing responses that mix secrets with attacker-controlled input over TLS (BREACH attack)
Interview Point: Q1 Which header does the server use to say how it compressed? Q2 Why not compress images? Q3 Why add Vary: Accept-Encoding?

chapters.title: Problem Details (RFC 9457) Errors
points: Problem Details: a standard JSON error body served as Content-Type: application/problem+json (XML variant: application/problem+xml); obsoletes RFC 7807

Standard members: type (URI identifying the error kind, default about:blank), title (short, stable summary), status (HTTP code), detail (this occurrence, human-readable), instance (URI of this occurrence)
Example: {"type":"https://api.example.com/errors/out-of-credit","title":"Out of credit","status":403,"detail":"Balance is 30, cost is 50.","instance":"/account/12345/txn/abc"}
Extension members add machine-readable data, e.g. "balance": 30 or an "errors" array of field violations for 422 validation failures; clients must ignore unknown members
Mistakes: status in body must match the HTTP status line; do not leak stack traces or internals in detail; do not parse title/detail for logic, switch on type; keep type stable
Interview Point: Q1 Which media type carries Problem Details? Q2 Difference between title and detail? Q3 How do you return multiple validation errors?

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Negotiation and Errors
points: Request headers: Accept (want), Accept-Encoding (can decode), Content-Type (body I am sending); response: Content-Type, Content-Encoding, Vary
Wrong Accept = 406; wrong request Content-Type = 415; malformed body that cannot be parsed = 400; body that parses but fails validation = 422
Accept: application/json, application/vnd.acme.v2+json;q=0.9, */*;q=0.1
Compress text with gzip/br, skip images and tiny payloads, always send Vary: Accept-Encoding
Errors: application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, instance plus extension members

Interview Point: Q1 Walk through a request negotiating format and compression end to end. Q2 What status for an unsupported body type? Q3 How would you design a consistent error format across services?
